name: IT University of Copenhagen
about: ITU is Denmark's smallest and youngest university, founded in 1999 and built around a single subject: information technology and what it does to people, business and society. Everything happens in one building in Ørestad in southern Copenhagen, so it feels much more like a large department than a campus university. All four bachelor's degrees have restricted admission and published GPA cut-offs, and only two of them are taught in English.
ibNotes: The IB has its own application deadline at ITU: 15 March, 12:00 noon CET, "regardless of quota or completion location".
ITU converts IB grades to the Danish 7-point scale; it gives IB grade 3 = Danish 2 and IB grade 5 = Danish 7 as worked examples.
The subject requirement 'Mathematics A' is met by Mathematics (HL), Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches (HL) or Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation (HL) — SL maths does not count.
The subject requirement 'English B' is met by English A1/A2 (HL or SL), English B (HL or SL) or English A: Language and Literature (HL or SL).
If you finish the IB the same year you apply, you must ask your IB coordinator to register you in IBIS by 1 May using ITU's institution code 003934.
quotaNotes: All ITU bachelor's degrees have restricted admission (adgangsbegrænsning) and are filled 80 per cent through quota 1 and 20 per cent through quota 2. Quota 1 is a straight GPA ranking against the published cut-off. Quota 2 looks at other criteria and ITU recommends attaching a motivational cover letter. Anyone with a foreign upper secondary exam — including the IB — must apply by the quota 2 deadline of 15 March, 12:00 noon CET.

deadlines.label: IBIS registration for applicants sitting the IB that year
deadlines.notes: Your IB coordinator must register you in IBIS with ITU's institution code 003934.

deadlines.label: Final documentation (European applicants)
deadlines.notes: Deadline for final documentation and for confirming the order of your programme preferences.

deadlines.label: Admission decisions
deadlines.notes: Decisions are sent by email; you must accept or decline by 30 July.

tuitionNonEu: EUR 8,250 per semester, EUR 49,500 for the full three-year programme (2026 admission). Application fee EUR 150. No scholarships are available at bachelor's level.

notes: ITU offers four bachelor's degrees but only two are taught in English. BSc Software Development is taught in Danish and requires Danish A; BSc Digital Design and Interactive Technologies is mainly Danish (only the second year is taught entirely in English) and also requires Danish A. Neither is listed here.

Read the Danish requirement carefully: BSc Global Business Informatics is taught in English but still demands Danish at A level as a passed subject, so in practice it is open only to applicants who have studied Danish. ITU's own BSc overview page says "only the programme in Data Science is open to international students".
BSc Data Science is the one ITU degree an IB student from outside Denmark can realistically enter — 73 per cent of the students admitted in 2026 were international.
ITU has a summer intake only; there is no February start at bachelor's level.

From the 2027 admission round ITU requires an overall GPA of at least 6.0 on the Danish 7-point scale for BSc Software Development. Check whether a similar floor has been added to the English-taught degrees before applying.

programmes.name: Data Science
programmes.summary: Three years of programming, mathematics, statistics and machine learning, taught with a lot of project work and an eye on what the data actually means for people. You do not need to have coded before. Graduates go into data science, machine learning engineering and analytics roles in finance, health, journalism and public planning.
programmes.requirementsText: A qualifying examination certificate equal to a Danish upper secondary school leaving certificate. Mathematics corresponding to the Danish A-level with an average mark of at least 6. English corresponding to the Danish B-level with an average mark of at least 6 (no grade requirement if you have passed English at Danish A-level).
extraRequirements: 100 students admitted in 2026; 595 applicants, of whom 417 applied in quota 2.
A motivational cover letter is recommended for quota 2 applicants.

programmes.name: Global Business Informatics
programmes.summary: A degree about how organisations actually use digital technology — AI, business analytics and digital transformation — rather than about building the technology itself. It is taught in English, but be warned: you must also have passed Danish at A level, so it is realistically only open to applicants who have Danish at A level — from a Danish gymnasium, or Danish A in the IB. Going to school in Denmark is not enough on its own.
programmes.requirementsText: A qualifying examination certificate that can be equated with a Danish upper secondary school leaving certificate. Mathematics corresponding to the Danish B-level with an average mark of at least 6. English corresponding to the Danish B-level with an average mark of at least 6. Danish at A level is a requirement. No required mark but the subject must be passed. You must be proficient in oral and written English, as the programme is taught in English. There is no grade requirement in Mathematics or English if you passed the subject at Danish A level.
extraRequirements: 71 study places in 2026; 92 per cent of those admitted had Danish qualifications.
Danish A must be passed even though teaching is in English.
